title: Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals, Eighth revised edition
publicationStatus: GHS 8 identity and chemicals-under-pressure criteria reviewed against rendered source pages; other Rev.8 changes are not incorporated automatically.
sourceKind: UN model GHS; supporting technical reference, not automatically binding under Canadian WHMIS.
legalPrecedence: Hazardous Products Act (HPA) and Hazardous Products Regulations (HPR, SOR/2015-17) govern; Health Canada interpretive guidance informs application. Only specified Rev.8 provisions should be used.

Changes to other physical hazard testing standards

chapterMap.note: Describes all Rev.8 amendment areas; only Canadian-adopted parts may be used.
Aerosols and chemicals under pressure are distinct classifications.
Aerosols: separate class; do not duplicate pressure class.
Definition: liquids/solids (including pastes/powders) pressurised with gas at >=200 kPa gauge at 20 °C; exclude aerosol dispensers and gases under pressure.
Flammable components are GHS flammable gases, liquids and solids.
Categories 1/2/3 thresholds: flammable component mass % and product heat of combustion kJ/g.
Do not include excluded pyrophoric, self-heating or water-reactive ingredients in a simplistic flammable summation; avoid duplicative classifications for section 2.3.1, Chapters 2.2, 2.5, 2.6, 2.7.
Symbols (Cat1/2 flame and cylinder; Cat3 cylinder); signal word Danger for Cat1 and Warning for Cat2/3.
Guidance diagram; use HPR-inclusive 200 kPa threshold, not conflicting >200 kPa prose in decision-tree box.
Specific heat of combustion formula: sum(mass_fraction_component × heat_of_combustion_component). Results need defensible measured/published/validated data.
Hazard codes H282 (Cat1), H283 (Cat2), H284 (Cat3) with pictograms.
Category-specific precautionary statements and conditions. HPR 3(1)(c.2) controls Canadian Category 3 hazard-statement wording.

scopePreconditions: Product is liquid or solid packaged in a receptacle (not an aerosol dispenser).
Product is pressurised with a gas, at >=200 kPa gauge at 20 °C.
Product is not classified as gases under pressure under HPR 7.5.
If already classified as Aerosols under HPR 7.3, HPR 7.21.1(1) prohibits Chemicals Under Pressure classification.
requiredInputs: whether qualifies as gases under pressure
classificationDecisionSpecification.notClassifiedIf: Does not meet Chemicals Under Pressure definition; assess other relevant physical hazards. Missing required evidence is UNDETERMINED, not NOT CLASSIFIED.
precedenceNotes: Canada's HPR controls at exactly 200 kPa gauge.
Category 1 and 2 categories are based on total flammable-component mass, not just the pressurising gas.
Other independent health and physical classes may remain applicable; check actual HPR hazard-class exclusions before suppression.

sourceIntegrityWarnings: The source text under GHS 2.3.2.2.1 refers to 'Table 2.3.2' but the actual chemicals-under-pressure criteria are Table 2.3.3 on printed page 62.
The diagram at printed page 63 uses 'higher than 200 kPa'; the GHS definition at 2.3.2.1 and Canadian HPR 7.21 use '200 kPa or more'. Implement inclusive >=200 kPa.
Source PDF embeds other material in text extraction; rely on rendered page visuals for tables, diagrams, and ambiguous extracted characters.
The 50%-liquid/solid versus 50%-gas example in GHS 2.3.2.1 is a typical-case NOTE, not an additional numerical legal criterion.
